assumptions: Source profile: ordinary transparent media with a real positive index at least one, plus vacuum.
Source condition: refractive index depends on optical wavelength and material conditions; use the supplied value for the selected mode and state.

gaps: Add phase_refractive_index; reuse wave_phase_speed from b01 with an optical-mode context. Units 1 and m/s exist. Phase/group distinction must survive any downstream binding.

models.inverse_notes: Inverse n=299792458/v requires 0<v<=299792458 in this n>=1 profile; one positive root, c remains fixed. v=149896229 m/s yields n=2 and forward substitution returns 149896229. Vacuum v=c yields n=1. v=0 has no finite index and v>c would leave this declared profile, though that is not a universal prohibition on phase velocity in other regimes.
limitations: The n>=1 scope is not a universal statement for anomalous-dispersion, plasma, complex-index or metamaterial phase velocities.
Phase speed is not automatically pulse/group speed or information speed; do not apply this record to a pulse travel time without additional support.

references.method: Published Example 1.1 reports 1.56e8 m/s, kept as expected. That example uses rounded c=3.00e8; the record uses exact SI c and gives about 1.55898e8. Difference about 1.02e5 m/s is within half the source's 1e6 m/s output increment (5e5). No empirical index uncertainty is claimed.
references.provenance: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-3/pages/1-1-the-propagation-of-light# Table 1.1 and Example 1.1; n at 589 nm vacuum wavelength

references.method: Definitional limiting identity: in vacuum the propagation speed is the SI defining c, independent of material data. Expected is exactly the NIST value; 1e-6 m/s only permits floating-point representation, not uncertainty in c.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero index is outside the ordinary-medium profile and makes the reciprocal undefined.
A material/state-specific refractive index is required; it is not assumed from a material label.

relationship.translation_notes: Solve n=c/v for v, resolving fixed c through the registry constant speed_of_light (runtime 0.28.0: exactly 299792458 m/s, SI defining constant), whose m/s dimensions are retained by the engine. Registry-named constants are not repeated in constants metadata or exposed as freely variable inputs; the exact SI value remains attributed to the unchanged NIST source. n is dimensionless, so (L*T^-1)/1=L*T^-1; m/s has base scale 1. 'Phase' identifies the refractive-index meaning, as opposed to group or signal speed. Source Table 1.1 explicitly ties indices to 589 nm vacuum wavelength and lists material-state conditions; those are reference data, not global defaults. Its blanket n>=1 prose is retained as this ordinary-medium profile, not asserted for every dispersive/anomalous medium.

sources.evidence: Index is vacuum light speed divided by material light speed. The section treats ordinary transparent media with n at least one and supplies wavelength-specific values; its zircon example reports 1.56e8 m/s from n=1.923.

models.summary: Refractive-index definition for ordinary transparent media in the source's n>=1 regime, using exact SI vacuum light speed. The material index remains supplied and state-specific.

variables.context: Same ordinary transparent homogeneous medium, wave mode/polarization where relevant, optical frequency (or vacuum wavelength), composition/phase, temperature, pressure and medium rest frame. n is the real phase refractive index for that state, and v the matching monochromatic phase speed; vacuum is the n=1 boundary.
variables.definition: Real phase refractive index: vacuum light speed divided by the monochromatic phase speed of the selected transparent-medium mode.
variables.domain: Finite n>=1 for this ordinary transparent-medium profile, including vacuum n=1; supplied at the matching optical frequency and material state.
